Mikael Backlund is 37, has spent his whole career with Calgary, and is still playing close to 19 minutes a night. The shots are coming: 62 in 24 games, with 6.06 expected goals, our measure of chance quality. He has three. Our numbers flag him as due, and the Flames have also scored 4.6 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice, so the luck is running against his linemates too. His last ten games produced one goal and three assists while his ice time went up.

The process looks like the Backlund you remember. Calgary has taken 51.9% of the five-on-five shot attempts with him out there, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 10.9 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 97th percentile among forwards, with plenty of scoring chances from in front of the net. Evolving-Hockey's 2025-26 numbers were mixed: around replacement level overall, but opponents got 0.12 fewer expected goals per 60 against him (88th percentile). Our numbers project 18 goals, and goals tend to follow chances like his.
headline: Backlund is due, and the Flames need him
